transcript.text: theres water in the bottom of my frige under the salad draws, keeps comming back after i mop it up

Water collecting under the salad drawers is most often caused by a blocked defrost drain hole. In frost-free fridges, condensation and defrost water should run down a small drain at the back into a tray underneath the appliance. If the drain blocks with food bits or ice, the water backs up into the bottom of the fridge.

Try this:

1. Turn the fridge off / unplug it if you can safely do so.
2. Take out the salad drawers and look at the back wall at the bottom of the fridge compartment. You may find a small hole or channel, sometimes hidden behind a cover.
3. Remove any visible debris and pour a little warm (not boiling) water into the drain.
4. Gently clear it using a pipe cleaner, soft flexible straw brush, or the cleaning tool supplied with some fridges. Avoid knives, wire coat hangers, or anything sharp—you could damage the drain tube.
5. If there is ice around the drain, let it fully thaw first. A hairdryer on a low setting, kept well away from water, can help, but allowing it to defrost naturally is safest.
6. Dry everything and switch it back on.

Also check:
• The door seal is clean and closing properly. A poor seal creates extra condensation.
• The fridge is not packed so tightly that food is pressed against the back wall.
• The fridge is slightly tilted backwards, not forwards, so water can run to the drain.

If it keeps returning after clearing the drain, or water is also appearing on the floor outside the fridge, the drain tube/tray may need professional cleaning or there may be a fault with the defrost system.

ok i took the draws out and theres a little groove with a hole at the bottom of the back wall, its full of bits of lettuce and gunk! i cleaned it with a cotton bud and warm water and the water went straight down. the water is only inside the frige by the way, nowhere near the plug. door seal looks ok and it seems level too

That sounds like you found the cause. The lettuce/gunk was blocking the defrost drain, so water had nowhere to go except into the bottom under the drawers.

Since warm water now runs straight down, you’ve likely fixed it. A few useful final steps:

• Flush the hole with a little more warm water—perhaps a cupful, slowly—to make sure the drain tube is fully clear.
• Wipe the groove and the area under the drawers dry.
• Put the drawers back and keep an eye on it over the next day or two.
• Avoid pushing loose leaves or packaging right against that back-bottom groove; wipe it out occasionally.

A small amount of water may appear once more if there was still pooled water or ice further back in the drain channel, but it should stop after that.
